measurement.name: Zeehan Current
measurement.range_interpretation: One approximate regional background value; no numerical uncertainty, range, confidence interval, annual extrema or seasonal observations supplied.
measurement.geographic_scope: Continental slope at the western entrance of Bass Strait; attributed historical estimate, not all western Tasmanian shelf flow.
measurement.section_orientation: Regional cross-current description; exact transverse axis and paired edges unresolved.
measurement.layer: Warm baroclinic slope-current context; fixed width depth bounds unresolved.
measurement.time_convention: Historical Baines et al. (1983) description repeated in Cresswell (2000); exact width occupation support unresolved.
measurement.boundary_rule: Attributed author approximate width; no numerical threshold or paired edge coordinates extracted.
measurement.source_citation: Cresswell, G. (2000), Currents of the continental shelf and upper slope of Tasmania, Papers and Proceedings of the Royal Society of Tasmania 133(3):21–30, doi:10.26749/rstpp.133.3.21.
measurement.source_locator: Introduction, printed p21 / PDF page 1, paragraph on Baines et al. (1983). Separate Strahan sections: pp24–25 and Figure 5C p28 / PDF page 8.
measurement.extraction_method: Approximate width from visually reviewed original paragraph; qualitative section comparison transcribed separately, no velocity-contour digitization.
measurement.phase_label: Attributed historical Bass Strait slope width
measurement.source_quality_note: The 40 km summary is attributed to Baines et al. (1983); March/December 1997 Strahan widths remain numerically unknown. Neither the survey depth nor later seasonal calendar supplies this width support.

original_regional_context.display_caption: Approximate 40 km historical slope-current width near western Bass Strait, attributed to Baines et al. (1983). Numerical uncertainty and paired edges unknown; not a 1997 Strahan section width.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: Separate 1997 Strahan evidence: December is described as narrower and slightly stronger than March. Neither section has a numerical width here. Two occupations do not establish annual extrema or a monthly climatology; 300 m ADCP coverage is not the historical width layer.
